claim: The COVID-19 pandemic originated in the Wuhan province of China in late 2019.
source: The COVID-19 pandemic originating in the Wuhan province of China in late 2019 has impacted global health, causing increased mortality among elderly patients and individuals with comorbid conditions.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as background information about the pandemic's origin.

claim: The COVID-19 pandemic has caused increased mortality among elderly patients and individuals with comorbid conditions.
source: The COVID-19 pandemic originating in the Wuhan province of China in late 2019 has impacted global health, causing increased mortality among elderly patients and individuals with comorbid conditions.
evidence: This is stated as an established fact about the pandemic's impact.

claim: SARS-CoV-2 has undergone mutations during its passage through affected populations.
source: During the passage of the virus through affected populations, it has undergone mutations, some of which have recently been linked with increased viral load and prognostic complexities.
evidence: This is stated as an observed phenomenon during the pandemic.

claim: Some SARS-CoV-2 mutations have been linked with increased viral load and prognostic complexities.
source: During the passage of the virus through affected populations, it has undergone mutations, some of which have recently been linked with increased viral load and prognostic complexities.
evidence: This is stated as a recent finding about certain mutations.

claim: Point mutations in SARS-CoV-2 are difficult to diagnose using qRT-PCR.
source: Several of these variants are point mutations that are difficult to diagnose using the gold standard quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) method and necessitates widespread sequencing which is expensive, has long turn-around times, and requires high viral load for calling mutations accurately.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the current gold standard diagnostic method.

claim: Sequencing for SARS-CoV-2 variant detection is expensive.
source: Several of these variants are point mutations that are difficult to diagnose using the gold standard quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) method and necessitates widespread sequencing which is expensive, has long turn-around times, and requires high viral load for calling mutations accurately.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of sequencing-based diagnostics.

claim: Sequencing for SARS-CoV-2 variant detection has long turn-around times.
source: Several of these variants are point mutations that are difficult to diagnose using the gold standard quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) method and necessitates widespread sequencing which is expensive, has long turn-around times, and requires high viral load for calling mutations accurately.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of sequencing-based diagnostics.

claim: Sequencing for SARS-CoV-2 variant detection requires high viral load for calling mutations accurately.
source: Several of these variants are point mutations that are difficult to diagnose using the gold standard quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) method and necessitates widespread sequencing which is expensive, has long turn-around times, and requires high viral load for calling mutations accurately.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of sequencing-based diagnostics.

claim: Francisella novicida Cas9 (FnCas9) has high specificity to identify mismatches in the target.
source: Here, we repurpose the high specificity of Francisella novicida Cas9 (FnCas9) to identify mismatches in the target for developing a lateral flow assay that can be successfully adapted for the simultaneous detection of SARS-CoV-2 infection as well as for detecting point mutations in the sequence of the virus obtained from patient samples.
evidence: This is stated as a property of FnCas9 that is being utilized in the study.

claim: A lateral flow assay using FnCas9 can simultaneously detect SARS-CoV-2 infection and point mutations.
source: Here, we repurpose the high specificity of Francisella novicida Cas9 (FnCas9) to identify mismatches in the target for developing a lateral flow assay that can be successfully adapted for the simultaneous detection of SARS-CoV-2 infection as well as for detecting point mutations in the sequence of the virus obtained from patient samples.
evidence: This is the main claim of the study describing the developed assay.

claim: The N501Y mutation is present across multiple variant lineages of SARS-CoV-2.
source: We report the detection of the S gene mutation N501Y (present across multiple variant lineages of SARS-CoV-2) within an hour using lateral flow paper strip chemistry.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the N501Y mutation.

claim: The N501Y mutation can be detected within an hour using lateral flow paper strip chemistry.
source: We report the detection of the S gene mutation N501Y (present across multiple variant lineages of SARS-CoV-2) within an hour using lateral flow paper strip chemistry.
evidence: This is a key finding of the study regarding the speed of detection.

claim: The RAY assay for N501Y detection was tested on 37 wild-type patient samples.
source: The results were corroborated using deep sequencing on multiple wild-type (n = 37) and mutant (n = 22) virus infected patient samples with a sensitivity of 87% and specificity of 97%.
evidence: This describes the sample size used for validation.

claim: The RAY assay for N501Y detection was tested on 22 mutant patient samples.
source: The results were corroborated using deep sequencing on multiple wild-type (n = 37) and mutant (n = 22) virus infected patient samples with a sensitivity of 87% and specificity of 97%.
evidence: This describes the sample size used for validation.

claim: The RAY assay for N501Y detection has a sensitivity of 87%.
source: The results were corroborated using deep sequencing on multiple wild-type (n = 37) and mutant (n = 22) virus infected patient samples with a sensitivity of 87% and specificity of 97%.
evidence: This is a quantitative performance metric from the study.

claim: The RAY assay for N501Y detection has a specificity of 97%.
source: The results were corroborated using deep sequencing on multiple wild-type (n = 37) and mutant (n = 22) virus infected patient samples with a sensitivity of 87% and specificity of 97%.
evidence: This is a quantitative performance metric from the study.

claim: The RAY design principle can be adapted for the E484K mutation.
source: The design principle can be rapidly adapted for other mutations (as shown also for E484K and T716I) highlighting the advantages of quick optimization and roll-out of CRISPR diagnostics (CRISPRDx) for disease surveillance even beyond COVID-19.
evidence: This is demonstrated in the study as evidence of adaptability.

claim: The RAY design principle can be adapted for the T716I mutation.
source: The design principle can be rapidly adapted for other mutations (as shown also for E484K and T716I) highlighting the advantages of quick optimization and roll-out of CRISPR diagnostics (CRISPRDx) for disease surveillance even beyond COVID-19.
evidence: This is demonstrated in the study as evidence of adaptability.

claim: The study was funded by Council for Scientific and Industrial Research, India.
source: This study was funded by Council for Scientific and Industrial Research, India.
evidence: This is stated as the funding source for the study.

claim: The coronavirus pandemic has affected about 157 million people worldwide.
source: Testing and isolating SARS-CoV-2-positive cases has been one of the main strategies for controlling the rise and spread of the coronavirus pandemic that has affected about 157 million people and 3 million deaths all over the world (World Health Organization, WHO).
evidence: This is cited from WHO data as of the time of writing.

claim: The coronavirus pandemic has caused 3 million deaths worldwide.
source: Testing and isolating SARS-CoV-2-positive cases has been one of the main strategies for controlling the rise and spread of the coronavirus pandemic that has affected about 157 million people and 3 million deaths all over the world (World Health Organization, WHO).
evidence: This is cited from WHO data as of the time of writing.

claim: The SARS-CoV-2 genome has undergone several mutations during its passage through the human host.
source: Like all other viruses, the SARS-CoV-2 genome has undergone several mutations during its passage through the human host, and the positive or negative impact of most of them on virus transmission and immune escape are still under investigation (Rabi et al., 2020; Pachetti et al., 2020; Korber et al., 2020; Zhou et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as an observed phenomenon with supporting citations.

claim: The positive or negative impact of most SARS-CoV-2 mutations on virus transmission and immune escape are still under investigation.
source: Like all other viruses, the SARS-CoV-2 genome has undergone several mutations during its passage through the human host, and the positive or negative impact of most of them on virus transmission and immune escape are still under investigation (Rabi et al., 2020; Pachetti et al., 2020; Korber et al., 2020; Zhou et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as the current state of research with supporting citations.

claim: In December 2020, health authorities in the United Kingdom reported the emergence of a new SARS-CoV-2 variant (lineage B.1.1.7).
source: In December 2020, health authorities in the United Kingdom had reported the emergence of a new SARS-CoV-2 variant (lineage B.1.1.7) that is phylogenetically distinct from other circulating strains in the region.
evidence: This is stated as a historical event in the pandemic.

claim: The B.1.1.7 variant is phylogenetically distinct from other circulating strains in the UK region.
source: In December 2020, health authorities in the United Kingdom had reported the emergence of a new SARS-CoV-2 variant (lineage B.1.1.7) that is phylogenetically distinct from other circulating strains in the region.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the B.1.1.7 variant.

claim: The B.1.1.7 variant has 23 mutations.
source: With 23 mutations, this variant had rapidly replaced former SARS-CoV-2 lineages occurring in the region and has been established to have greater transmissibility through modeling and clinical correlation studies (Chand, 2020; Horby et al., 2021; Davies et al., 2021; Volz et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the B.1.1.7 variant.

claim: The B.1.1.7 variant rapidly replaced former SARS-CoV-2 lineages in the UK region.
source: With 23 mutations, this variant had rapidly replaced former SARS-CoV-2 lineages occurring in the region and has been established to have greater transmissibility through modeling and clinical correlation studies (Chand, 2020; Horby et al., 2021; Davies et al., 2021; Volz et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as an observed phenomenon with supporting citations.

claim: The B.1.1.7 variant has been established to have greater transmissibility through modeling and clinical correlation studies.
source: With 23 mutations, this variant had rapidly replaced former SARS-CoV-2 lineages occurring in the region and has been established to have greater transmissibility through modeling and clinical correlation studies (Chand, 2020; Horby et al., 2021; Davies et al., 2021; Volz et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as an established finding with supporting citations.

claim: South African authorities reported the B.1.351 variant.
source: Subsequently, the South African and Brazilian authorities have also reported variants (B.1.351 and P.1, respectively) that have been associated with a higher viral load in preliminary studies (Tegally et al., 2020; Faria et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as a historical event with supporting citations.

claim: Brazilian authorities reported the P.1 variant.
source: Subsequently, the South African and Brazilian authorities have also reported variants (B.1.351 and P.1, respectively) that have been associated with a higher viral load in preliminary studies (Tegally et al., 2020; Faria et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as a historical event with supporting citations.

claim: The B.1.351 and P.1 variants have been associated with a higher viral load in preliminary studies.
source: Subsequently, the South African and Brazilian authorities have also reported variants (B.1.351 and P.1, respectively) that have been associated with a higher viral load in preliminary studies (Tegally et al., 2020; Faria et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from preliminary studies with supporting citations.

claim: Till May 2021, at least 13 emerging SARS-CoV-2 lineages with multiple mutations have been reported from sequencing efforts across the globe.
source: Till May 2021, at least 13 emerging SARS-CoV-2 lineages with multiple mutations have been reported from sequencing efforts across the globe (CDC, 2021).
evidence: This is stated as a fact from CDC data as of May 2021.

claim: SARS-CoV-2 variants are classified as either Variants of Concern (VOC) or Variants of Interest (VOI).
source: Variants in lineages of the SARS-CoV-2 genome have been classified either as Variants of Concern (VOC) or Variants of Interest (VOI).
evidence: This is stated as the classification system for variants.

claim: VOCs have shown an indication of higher severity, transmissibility, and impact on pandemic spread from ongoing studies.
source: Among these, the VOCs have shown an indication of higher severity, transmissibility, and impact on pandemic spread from ongoing studies.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of VOCs based on ongoing research.

claim: VOIs have limited evidence for higher severity and transmissibility currently but are being monitored for potential impact in the future.
source: VOIs have limited evidence for the same currently but are being monitored for potential impact in the future.
evidence: This is stated as the current status of VOIs.

claim: Till May 2021, at least five lineages (B.1.1.7, P.1, B.1.351, B.1.427, and B.1.429) have been classified as VOCs.
source: Till May 2021, at least five lineages (B.1.1.7, P.1, B.1.351, B.1.427, and B.1.429) have been classified as VOCs and are being investigated for their susceptibility to diagnosis, response to vaccines, and correlation with disease severity and transmission (CDC, 2021).
evidence: This is stated as a fact from CDC data as of May 2021.

claim: VOCs are being investigated for their susceptibility to diagnosis, response to vaccines, and correlation with disease severity and transmission.
source: Till May 2021, at least five lineages (B.1.1.7, P.1, B.1.351, B.1.427, and B.1.429) have been classified as VOCs and are being investigated for their susceptibility to diagnosis, response to vaccines, and correlation with disease severity and transmission (CDC, 2021).
evidence: This is stated as ongoing research activities with supporting citation.

claim: Infected individuals harboring SARS-CoV-2 mutations have been detected in countries far away from their origin as air travel has resumed.
source: As air travel has resumed in most countries post lockdown, infected individuals harboring these mutations have been detected in countries far away from their origin, generating concerns about greater disease incidence unless these cases are recognized and isolated.
evidence: This is stated as an observed phenomenon following resumption of air travel.

claim: Vaccine roll-out has been initiated in several countries.
source: That is particularly important as vaccine roll-out has been initiated in several countries, and the studies about vaccine efficacy against the new variants are only in their infancy.
evidence: This is stated as a fact about the pandemic response.

claim: Studies about vaccine efficacy against the new SARS-CoV-2 variants are only in their infancy.
source: That is particularly important as vaccine roll-out has been initiated in several countries, and the studies about vaccine efficacy against the new variants are only in their infancy.
evidence: This is stated as the current state of research on vaccine efficacy.

claim: qRT-PCR has been the most widely adopted nucleic-acid-based test for identifying coronavirus infected cases.
source: Among the diagnostic methods that have been employed for identifying coronavirus infected cases, qRT-PCR has been the most widely adopted nucleic-acid-based test due to its ability to identify even low copy numbers of viral RNA in patient samples and has been considered as a gold standard in diagnosis (Mackay, 2002; Carter et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as a fact about diagnostic methods with supporting citations.

claim: qRT-PCR can identify even low copy numbers of viral RNA in patient samples.
source: Among the diagnostic methods that have been employed for identifying coronavirus infected cases, qRT-PCR has been the most widely adopted nucleic-acid-based test due to its ability to identify even low copy numbers of viral RNA in patient samples and has been considered as a gold standard in diagnosis (Mackay, 2002; Carter et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of qRT-PCR with supporting citations.

claim: qRT-PCR has been considered as a gold standard in diagnosis for SARS-CoV-2.
source: Among the diagnostic methods that have been employed for identifying coronavirus infected cases, qRT-PCR has been the most widely adopted nucleic-acid-based test due to its ability to identify even low copy numbers of viral RNA in patient samples and has been considered as a gold standard in diagnosis (Mackay, 2002; Carter et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as the status of qRT-PCR with supporting citations.

claim: Probe-based qRT PCR assays are generally not suited for genotyping point mutations associated with novel CoV2 variants.
source: However, probe-based qRT PCR assays rely on amplification of a target gene with real-time analysis of DNA copy numbers and are generally not suited for genotyping point mutations associated with novel CoV2 variants (Afzal, 2020; Yin, 2020; Vandenberg et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of qRT-PCR with supporting citations.

claim: ARMS-qPCR has been described in the literature for genotyping mutations in nucleic acids.
source: Although strategies such as Amplification Refractory Mutation System-quantitative PCR (ARMS-qPCR) have been described in the literature for genotyping mutations in nucleic acids, these require substantial design and validation for reproducible readouts and hence are not routinely used for clinical diagnosis (Little, 2001).
evidence: This is stated as an existing method with supporting citation.

claim: ARMS-qPCR requires substantial design and validation for reproducible readouts.
source: Although strategies such as Amplification Refractory Mutation System-quantitative PCR (ARMS-qPCR) have been described in the literature for genotyping mutations in nucleic acids, these require substantial design and validation for reproducible readouts and hence are not routinely used for clinical diagnosis (Little, 2001).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of ARMS-qPCR with supporting citation.

claim: ARMS-qPCR is not routinely used for clinical diagnosis.
source: Although strategies such as Amplification Refractory Mutation System-quantitative PCR (ARMS-qPCR) have been described in the literature for genotyping mutations in nucleic acids, these require substantial design and validation for reproducible readouts and hence are not routinely used for clinical diagnosis (Little, 2001).
evidence: This is stated as the current usage status of ARMS-qPCR with supporting citation.

claim: Antigen-based SARS-CoV-2 assays have lower sensitivity than qPCR.
source: Similarly, antigen-based SARS-CoV-2 assays which have lower sensitivity than qPCR have not yet been reported to specifically identify mutant variants.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of antigen-based assays.

claim: Antigen-based SARS-CoV-2 assays have not yet been reported to specifically identify mutant variants.
source: Similarly, antigen-based SARS-CoV-2 assays which have lower sensitivity than qPCR have not yet been reported to specifically identify mutant variants.
evidence: This is stated as the current status of antigen-based assays.

claim: Most countries have resorted to next-generation sequencing of patient samples for understanding the evolution of mutations in the virus and detecting variants in suspected individuals.
source: In the absence of any true diagnostic test for the variants, most countries have resorted to next-generation sequencing of patient samples both for understanding the evolution of mutations in the virus as well as detecting the variants in suspected individuals (Vandenberg et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as the current practice with supporting citation.

claim: Using sequencing for routine diagnosis greatly increases both the time and cost of identifying positive individuals.
source: Using sequencing for routine diagnosis greatly increases both the time and cost of identifying positive individuals (Jayamohan et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of sequencing with supporting citation.

claim: CRISPR diagnostics (CRISPRDx) have been documented for identifying CoV2 signatures in patient samples.
source: We and several others have documented the applicability of CRISPR diagnostics (CRISPRDx) for identifying CoV2 signatures in patient samples (Broughton et al., 2020; Patchsung et al., 2020; Ding et al., 2020; Joung et al., 2020; Fozouni et al., 2021; Guo et al., 2020; Lucia et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2021; Azhar et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as prior work with multiple supporting citations.

claim: The FELUDA platform for SARS-CoV-2 diagnosis has similar accuracy as the gold standard qPCR test.
source: Using the Cas9 from Francisella novicida (FnCas9), we have recently reported the development of the FELUDA (FnCas9 Editor Linked Uniform Detection Assay) platform for SARS-CoV-2 diagnosis with similar accuracy as the gold standard qPCR test (Azhar et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from prior work with supporting citation.

claim: The FELUDA assay is performed on a Lateral Flow strip and generates a visual readout within an hour.
source: The assay which is performed on a Lateral Flow strip generates a visual readout within an hour that is quantifiable using a smartphone-based application.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the FELUDA assay.

claim: The FELUDA assay readout is quantifiable using a smartphone-based application.
source: The assay which is performed on a Lateral Flow strip generates a visual readout within an hour that is quantifiable using a smartphone-based application.
evidence: This is stated as a feature of the FELUDA assay.

claim: FnCas9 has a very high intrinsic specificity to point mismatches in the target.
source: Since FnCas9 has a very high intrinsic specificity to point mismatches in the target (Acharya et al., 2019), we speculated that the enzyme can also be used for detecting SARS-CoV-2 variants on a paper strip with high accuracy.
evidence: This is stated as a property of FnCas9 with supporting citation.

claim: RAY can successfully detect both SARS-CoV-2 infection and the presence of the common N501Y mutation.
source: RAY can successfully detect both SARS-CoV-2 infection as well as the presence of the common N501Y mutation present across the majority of VOCs described so far and distinguish it from the parent CoV2 lineage.
evidence: This is stated as a key finding of the study.

claim: RAY can distinguish the N501Y mutation from the parent CoV2 lineage.
source: RAY can successfully detect both SARS-CoV-2 infection as well as the presence of the common N501Y mutation present across the majority of VOCs described so far and distinguish it from the parent CoV2 lineage.
evidence: This is stated as a key finding of the study.

claim: RAY can be employed as a primary surveillance method for isolating cases belonging to VOC groups.
source: Thus, it can be employed as a primary surveillance method for isolating cases belonging to these groups and can enable the initiation of appropriate management protocols.
evidence: This is stated as a potential application of RAY.

claim: FnCas9 is unable to bind or cleave targets having two mismatches at the 2nd and 6th position (PAM proximal) of the sgRNA.
source: In an earlier study, we had successfully established that FnCas9 is unable to bind or cleave targets having two mismatches at the 2nd and 6th position (PAM proximal) of the sgRNA with respect to the target (Azhar et al., 2021; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from prior work with supporting citation and figure reference.

claim: FnCas9 is unable to bind or cleave targets having two mismatches at the 16th and 19th position (PAM distal).
source: Through in vitro cleavage studies of a double-stranded DNA substrate, we identified that the same outcome is also observed when mismatches are present at the 16th and 19th position (PAM distal) (Figure 1A, Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated as a new finding from in vitro cleavage studies with figure reference.

claim: Out of the 48 unique SNVs reported across all VOCs and VOIs, 19 SNVs can be targeted by RAY.
source: We found that out of the 48 unique SNVs reported across all the VOCs and VOIs reported so far (CDC, 2021), 19 SNVs (12 VOC-associated SNVs and 7 VOI-associated SNVs) can be targeted by RAY (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from analysis of reported SNVs with supporting citation.

claim: 12 VOC-associated SNVs can be targeted by RAY.
source: We found that out of the 48 unique SNVs reported across all the VOCs and VOIs reported so far (CDC, 2021), 19 SNVs (12 VOC-associated SNVs and 7 VOI-associated SNVs) can be targeted by RAY (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from analysis with supporting citation.

claim: 7 VOI-associated SNVs can be targeted by RAY.
source: We found that out of the 48 unique SNVs reported across all the VOCs and VOIs reported so far (CDC, 2021), 19 SNVs (12 VOC-associated SNVs and 7 VOI-associated SNVs) can be targeted by RAY (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from analysis with supporting citation.

claim: Each VOC/VOI reported so far consists of at least one of the 19 SNVs targetable by RAY.
source: Interestingly, each VOC/VOI reported so far consists of at least one of the 19 SNVs and can therefore be targeted by RAY design (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from analysis with figure reference.

claim: N501Y is present across 3/5 of the VOCs (B.1.1.7, P.1, and B.1.351).
source: Among these SNVs, N501Y is present across 3/5 of the VOCs (B.1.1.7, P.1, and B.1.351).
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the N501Y mutation.

claim: The N501Y mutation affects the receptor-binding domain of the virus.
source: This mutation affects the receptor-binding domain of the virus and is the subject of numerous studies analyzing the efficacy of vaccines against the mutated form of the virus (Cheng et al., 2021; Dejnirattisai et al., 2021; Ku et al., 2021; Luan et al., 2021; Naveca et al., 2021; Tian et al., 2021; Xie et al., 2021; Collier et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of N501Y with supporting citations.

claim: The N501Y mutation is the subject of numerous studies analyzing the efficacy of vaccines against the mutated form of the virus.
source: This mutation affects the receptor-binding domain of the virus and is the subject of numerous studies analyzing the efficacy of vaccines against the mutated form of the virus (Cheng et al., 2021; Dejnirattisai et al., 2021; Ku et al., 2021; Luan et al., 2021; Naveca et al., 2021; Tian et al., 2021; Xie et al., 2021; Collier et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as the current research focus with supporting citations.

claim: Catalytically active FnCas9 was able to successfully cleave the dsDNA substrate containing the N501Y mutation while leaving the WT sequence intact.
source: We found that catalytically active FnCas9 was able to successfully cleave the dsDNA substrate containing the N501Y mutation while leaving the WT sequence intact (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with figure reference.

claim: The RAY approach for variant identification can be performed using a stand-alone or portable electrophoresis apparatus.
source: We established that this approach for variant identification can be performed using a stand-alone or portable electrophoresis apparatus leading to a turnaround time of about 1.5 hr from RNA to read-out (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the method with figure reference.

claim: The electrophoresis-based RAY has a turnaround time of about 1.5 hr from RNA to read-out.
source: We established that this approach for variant identification can be performed using a stand-alone or portable electrophoresis apparatus leading to a turnaround time of about 1.5 hr from RNA to read-out (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated as a performance metric with figure reference.

claim: Dye-based systems have inherent low sensitivity and cannot be used for routine diagnosis.
source: However, dye-based systems have inherent low sensitivity and cannot be used for routine diagnosis.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of dye-based detection systems.

claim: A catalytically inactive (dead) FnCas9 can be used to accurately identify the presence of SARS-CoV-2 RNA in patient samples using a lateral flow assay.
source: In an earlier study, we had reported that using a lateral flow assay, a catalytically inactive (dead) FnCas9 generated by mutating the RuvC and HNH domains can be used to accurately identify the presence of SARS-CoV-2 RNA in patient samples (Azhar et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from prior work with supporting citation.

claim: An amplicon of 580 bp gave a clear discernible signal distinguishing the N501Y mutation over the WT sample.
source: Among the four amplicon sizes that we investigated, an amplicon of 580 bp gave a clear discernible signal distinguishing the N501Y mutation over the WT sample (Figure 3A, Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with figure reference.

claim: RAY was able to correctly identify the variant signature in all eight samples that harbored the N501Y mutation.
source: RAY was able to correctly identify the variant signature in all eight samples that harbored the mutation (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result with figure reference.

claim: Samples with low viral load (qRT-PCR Ct >25) showed a comparatively faint band in single amplicon RAY.
source: In particular, samples with low viral load (qRT-PCR Ct >25) showed a comparatively faint band (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from experiments with figure reference.

claim: RAY correctly classified all eight WT samples where neither the N501Y mutation nor any other lineage variants were present.
source: Importantly, RAY correctly classified all eight WT samples where neither the N501Y mutation nor any other lineage variants were present as seen by either an absence of a distinct band or an extremely faint band in the test line (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result with figure reference.

claim: RAY identified all confirmed COVID-19-negative samples (12) tested.
source: In addition, RAY identified all confirmed COVID-19-negative samples (12) tested simultaneously (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result with figure reference.

claim: TOPSE is a smartphone-based application that generates a band intensity score from a lateral flow strip.
source: Firstly, we used TOPSE (True Outcome Predicted via Strip Evaluation), a smartphone-based application to generate a band intensity score from a lateral flow strip to eliminate bias that can result from visual estimation (Appendix 1).
evidence: This is stated as a tool used in the study.

claim: Double biotinylation increased the test band intensity for the 580 bp amplicon by 1.5 times compared to single biotin-labeled amplicon.
source: We observed that upon double biotinylation the test band intensity for the 580 bp amplicon was 1.5 times higher than single biotin-labeled amplicon (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with figure reference.

claim: Amplicons with shorter lengths had higher band intensities within the same sample.
source: To increase the band intensity further, we reduced the length of the PCR amplicon containing the N501Y mutation and found that within the same sample, amplicons with shorter lengths had higher band intensities (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with figure reference.

claim: With an amplicon size of 149 bp, a clearly discernible background-corrected signal intensity could be achieved in the mutant sample over the WT sample.
source: In particular, with an amplicon size of 149 bp, a clearly discernible background-corrected signal intensity could be achieved in the mutant sample over the WT sample (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with figure reference.

claim: The double amplicon RAY assay has a reduced overall time for completion (55 min) compared to single amplicon RAY (75 min).
source: The double amplicon RAY assay results in shorter products and lower overall time for completion, starting from RNA samples while compared to a single amplicon RAY (reduced to 55 min from 75 min).
evidence: This is stated as a performance improvement.

claim: RAY was able to give a clearly discernible SN501Y sgRNA signal that was at least 5.5 times higher than that of the WT sample up to a Ct value of 34.
source: We observed that RAY was able to give a clearly discernible SN501Y sgRNA signal that was at least 5.5 times higher than that of the WT sample up to a Ct value of 34.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding from sensitivity testing.

claim: RAY is sufficiently sensitive in detecting the N501Y VOC in a sample with only a few copies of the virus and is comparable to other sequencing platforms.
source: Taken together, RAY is sufficiently sensitive in detecting the N501Y VOC in a sample with only a few copies of the virus and is comparable to other sequencing platforms (Klempt et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from sensitivity testing with supporting citation.

claim: SN501Y was able to detect 36/37 WT samples in the validation study.
source: With a single run of the assay, SN501Y was able to detect 36/37 WT samples and 19/22 N501Y samples corresponding to a sensitivity of 86% and a specificity of 97% across all ranges of Ct values (Figure 4F, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is stated as a result from the validation study with figure reference.

claim: SN501Y was able to detect 19/22 N501Y samples in the validation study.
source: With a single run of the assay, SN501Y was able to detect 36/37 WT samples and 19/22 N501Y samples corresponding to a sensitivity of 86% and a specificity of 97% across all ranges of Ct values (Figure 4F, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is stated as a result from the validation study with figure reference.

claim: Amplicons containing the E484K mutation do not show cross-reactivity with the N501Y sgRNA.
source: Importantly, amplicons containing the E484K mutation do not show cross-reactivity with the N501Y sgRNA, highlighting the specificity of the assay between variants (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with figure reference.
